title: A systematic review of intelligent and robot tutoring systems: evolution, pedagogical design, and AI-driven classification
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how tutoring systems have evolved from early computer-assisted instruction to modern intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) and robot tutoring systems (RTS), with particular attention to AI techniques, pedagogical design, adaptability, engagement, and ethics. The review asks how these systems support personalized learning, which technological advances have been most important, and what ethical and implementation challenges remain.

The intervention studied is not a single program but the broader class of tutoring technologies, including software-based ITS, robot-based RTS, and multimodal systems. Using a PRISMA-guided systematic review of 86 representative studies drawn from 1972 to 2024, the authors coded studies across dimensions including AI technique, adaptability, interaction mode, feedback type, engagement, and ethical concerns. They also conducted a latent class analysis that identified three system categories: computer-based ITS, verbal robot-based systems, and multimodal tutoring systems.

The population represented across the reviewed studies was mixed across educational levels and subject areas. The review reports that 38% of systems were implemented in higher education, 27% in secondary schools, 21% in primary schools, and 14% in lifelong or informal learning contexts. Most studies focused on students, especially in STEM and language learning settings, with deployment spanning multiple contexts over more than five decades rather than one specific site or country.

The main conclusions are that tutoring systems have become increasingly sophisticated, especially through AI methods such as Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, NLP, and large language models. ITS generally show stronger cognitive adaptability and instructional personalization, while RTS are stronger for social and emotional engagement but lag in cognitive adaptivity. The review also finds important unresolved issues around scalability, equitable access, privacy, bias, and responsible AI safeguards, and argues that future hybrid systems should better integrate cognitive support with socio-emotional engagement.

identified_tools.name: ITS
identified_tools.description: Computer-based intelligent tutoring systems that provide instructional support through learner modeling, adaptive sequencing, and automated feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of tutoring systems research from 1972–2024. This category covers software-based tutoring systems across educational settings; the review compares their pedagogical features, personalization, engagement, scalability, and ethical considerations without a uniform comparator or pooled effect estimate.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature, software-based ITS are characterized as supporting personalized and adaptive instruction and are generally associated with improved learning processes and academic outcomes, although no pooled effect size is reported in this review.
findings.measure: Learning outcomes / academic performance in reviewed ITS studies

findings.finding_summary: The review describes ITS as supporting cognitive engagement through adaptive content and immediate feedback, while noting weaker support for social and emotional forms of engagement than more embodied systems.
findings.measure: Cognitive engagement and motivation in reviewed ITS studies

findings.finding_summary: The review presents software-based ITS as comparatively easier to deploy and scale than robot-based systems because they can run on existing digital infrastructure and do not require specialized hardware.
The review identifies ongoing concerns for ITS related to data privacy, fairness, and responsible AI use, alongside continued technical limitations in achieving richer forms of adaptation.

identified_tools.name: Robot tutoring systems
identified_tools.description: Embodied tutoring systems that use physical robots to provide instructional support through speech, gestures, and other social or multimodal interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of tutoring systems research from 1972–2024. This category covers robot-based tutoring systems across educational settings; the review synthesizes evidence on social-emotional engagement, pedagogical effectiveness, adaptability, scalability, and ethical considerations without a uniform comparator or pooled effect estimate.

findings.finding_summary: The review describes robot tutoring systems as promising for motivation, social interaction, and social-emotional aspects of learning, particularly through physical presence and human-like interaction.
findings.measure: Motivation, social-emotional learning, and emotional engagement

findings.finding_summary: The review indicates that robot tutoring systems can support learning and problem-solving, but they are generally described as offering less sophisticated cognitive adaptation and personalization than software-based ITS.
findings.measure: Academic performance and adaptive instructional support

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature, robot tutoring systems are described as supporting participation, engagement, and positive attitudes toward learning through multimodal social interaction.
findings.measure: Engagement, participation, and attitudes toward learning

findings.finding_summary: The review identifies deployment and scalability constraints for robot tutoring systems due to hardware, maintenance, and classroom integration requirements.
findings.measure: Scalability, deployment complexity, and maintenance burden

findings.finding_summary: The review notes ethical and implementation concerns for robot tutoring systems, including privacy, transparency, and questions about sustained human-robot interaction in educational settings.
findings.measure: Ethical concerns related to privacy, transparency, and human-robot interaction

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: Generative AI chatbot that produces and revises natural-language text, answers prompts, and provides writing support through conversational interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: The review cites ChatGPT as an example of a modern AI model integrated into tutoring systems. It is discussed at the framework level as part of the evolution toward interactive, conversational tutoring experiences that provide real-time feedback and adaptive interactions tailored to learner needs. The paper does not tie ChatGPT to a specific intervention study outcome within the review text provided.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review using PRISMA procedures and explicit coding/reliability methods, which is stronger than a single observational study. However, it is not a quantitative meta-analysis of effect sizes, and the evidence synthesis includes heterogeneous studies with limited reporting on implementation and outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The review concludes that tutoring systems generally show promise for learning, engagement, and personalization, but it does not provide a pooled effect size or a clear quantified estimate of impact. Because effects are described as positive but heterogeneous and often unclear across system types, impact is best classified as modest or unclear.
